bg.understandDesc: Zero-emission vehicles run solely on clean energy such as electricity or hydrogen, emitting no air pollutants while driving. Start with their environmental, economic, and safety advantages.
bg.compareDesc: Among the 100+ electric and hydrogen models sold in Korea, compare vehicles by price, range, and charging time to find the one that fits your lifestyle and driving patterns.
bg.buyDesc: Combining national and local subsidies with tax reductions can save you up to 13.5 million KRW. Check your local government's budget status first.
bg.manageDesc: Everything you need for daily driving: the two-year mandatory operation period, charging card issuance, home and public charging, and battery care.
bg.checklistDescHtml:
The key questions and answers users ask most,
right before buying a zero-emission vehicle.
bg.q1: Can I charge an EV at home?
bg.q1a: If you live in an apartment complex, check with the management office whether slow chargers are installed. If not, you can apply directly for shared slow-charger installation with the residents' council's consent and receive an installation subsidy.
bg.q2a: Most EVs sold in Korea today drive 300–500 km per charge, and the hydrogen NEXO exceeds 600 km. Considering the average daily drive of 40–50 km, that is more than enough.
bg.q3: How much will I actually get when buying?
bg.q3a: As of 2026, national subsidies for passenger EVs reach up to 6.5 million KRW, with local subsidies averaging 3.5–7 million KRW — 10–13.5 million KRW in total. On top of that come tax reductions: 1.4 million KRW acquisition tax, 3 million KRW individual consumption tax, education tax, and more.
evcar.title: What is an Electric Vehicle?
evcar.intro: An electric vehicle (EV) runs on an electric motor powered by energy stored in a battery, with no internal combustion engine. Because it emits no air pollutants or greenhouse gases while driving, it has become the centerpiece of eco-friendly mobility.
evcar.howItWorks: An EV consists mainly of a battery, electric motor, reducer, inverter, and charger. The inverter converts direct current (DC) stored in the high-voltage battery into alternating current (AC) to drive the motor, and during deceleration, regenerative braking converts kinetic energy back into electricity stored in the battery.
evcar.type1: Passenger EVs (BEV) — Hyundai IONIQ 5/6, Kia EV6/EV9, Tesla Model 3/Y, Hyundai Kona Electric, and more
evcar.type2: Electric trucks — Hyundai Porter EV, Kia Bongo EV; the compact 1-ton delivery market is growing fast
evcar.type3: Electric motorcycles — centered on delivery platforms, with battery-swapping models expanding
evcar.type4: Electric buses — deployed mainly on city and village routes, accelerating in Seoul, Busan, and other major cities
evcar.type5: Electric construction machinery — excavators, forklifts, and more entering eco-friendly construction sites
evcar.charging: Charging is divided by speed into slow (AC, ~7 kW), fast (DC, 50–100 kW), and ultra-fast (DC, 350 kW and above). Slow charging takes 6–8 hours at home or work, while fast charging reaches 80% within 30 minutes at highway rest areas and public stations. Ultra-fast charging takes only around 10–20 minutes.
evcar.pro1: Environment — zero tailpipe emissions, directly improving urban air quality
evcar.pro2: Economy — annual running costs 70–90% lower than comparable combustion vehicles
evcar.pro3: Quietness — no engine noise, so cabin noise is remarkably low
evcar.pro4: Tax benefits — up to 5.3 million KRW off acquisition, individual consumption, and education taxes
evcar.pro5: Subsidies — up to 13.5 million KRW in combined national and local government support
evcar.notes: Before buying an EV, check your local government's remaining subsidy budget first, and keep the two-year mandatory operation period to avoid subsidy clawback. Detailed range, subsidy, and charging-time figures by model are available in the vehicle comparison tool.
h2car.title: What is a Hydrogen Vehicle?
h2car.intro: A fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) generates electricity by reacting hydrogen with oxygen from the air in a fuel cell, and uses that electricity to drive its motor. Its only emission is pure water (H₂O) — it even purifies the air it takes in, earning it the nickname 'an air purifier on wheels.'
h2car.howItWorks: When high-pressure hydrogen gas from the tank is supplied to the fuel cell stack, it reacts electrochemically with oxygen in the air to produce electricity, heat, and water. The electricity drives the motor or is stored in an auxiliary battery, while the water is released as vapor through the exhaust.
h2car.charging: Hydrogen refueling uses two pressure standards: 700 bar for passenger cars and 350 bar for commercial vehicles. Refueling takes about five minutes for a passenger car — similar to refueling a gasoline vehicle — and one fill provides over 600 km of range.
h2car.model1: Hyundai NEXO — Korea's flagship hydrogen passenger car, 609 km per fill
h2car.model2: Hyundai ELEC CITY Fuel Cell bus — commercial model for city and express routes, expanding across major cities
h2car.model3: Hyundai XCIENT Fuel Cell truck — a key carbon-neutral vehicle for logistics and freight
h2car.pro1: Fast refueling — full in under 5 minutes, the same experience as refueling gasoline
h2car.pro2: Long range — over 600 km per fill, ideal for long-distance driving
h2car.pro3: Air purification — filters the air it takes in while driving, improving air quality
h2car.pro4: Heavy loads — stronger than battery EVs for commercial trucks and buses
h2car.pro5: Government support — up to 22.5 million KRW in purchase subsidies plus tax reductions
h2car.infra: 145 hydrogen stations are in operation nationwide, expanding mainly around the Seoul metropolitan and Yeongnam regions. Station outages and maintenance schedules can be checked in real time at the Hydrogen Station Help Desk, which also guides you to alternative stations during outages.
h2car.notes: Hydrogen refueling infrastructure is still more limited than EV charging, so it is important to check station locations along your home and main routes in advance. Hydrogen vehicles are especially well suited to long commutes and long-haul freight.
battery.title: All About EV Batteries
battery.intro: The battery is the heart of an electric vehicle. Today's lithium-ion batteries are designed with high energy density and efficiency for long-distance driving, and how you manage them greatly affects their lifespan and performance.
battery.type1: Ternary (NCM/NCA) — nickel-cobalt-manganese based; high energy density, mainly used in long-range EVs
battery.type2: Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) — excellent cost and safety; adoption expanding in the Tesla Model 3 Standard and mid-priced models
battery.type3: Solid-state batteries — next-generation technology expected after 2027, improving both energy density and safety
battery.life: EV batteries are generally designed to retain 70–80% of their initial capacity for 8–10 years or about 160,000 km. Most manufacturers offer an 8-year/160,000 km warranty, with free replacement if performance falls below the threshold within the warranty period.
battery.tip1: State of charge — keep between 20–80% in daily use; avoid repeated deep discharges and full charges
battery.tip2: Temperature — manage heat shielding when parked long in extreme heat or cold; avoid direct summer sunlight
battery.tip3: Fast-charging frequency — rely mainly on slow charging; use fast charging only for long trips
battery.tip4: Long-term parking — store at 50–60% charge if unused for two weeks or more
battery.recycle: The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment operates a recycling system for used EV batteries. After performance evaluation at resource circulation centers, used batteries are routed to reuse (ESS/energy storage) or recycling (recovering lithium, nickel, and cobalt). Vehicles purchased with individual subsidies since 2021 have no battery return obligation — the battery is owned and transferred with the vehicle.
battery.safety: Interest in battery fire safety has been growing. The government enforces safety guidelines including overcharge prevention, safety standards for charging facilities in underground parking, and regular BMS (battery management system) inspections. Detailed standards are available in the relevant regulations and guidelines.
battery.diag: Manufacturer and charging-operator apps show your battery's state of health (SOH) and any abnormal cells in real time. Batteries at or below 80% SOH qualify for warranty replacement, while those below 60% are classified as unfit for reuse.
